<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a standard, clean package build script. It downloads prebuilt tar.zst archives from the project's own GitHub releases (github.com/VitaminDB/synshell), verifies sha256 checksums, and extracts them using bsdtar into $pkgdir. The package() function merely extracts the bundled binary archive — there are no eval, curl|bash, wget|bash, or other suspicious commands. The checksums are provided (not SKIP), the source URLs are the project's upstream releases, and the build logic follows ordinary AUR packaging practices. No code exfiltrates local data, no backdoors or reverse shells are present, and there is no obfuscated or encoded commands intended to hide malicious intent.
</details>

This is a standard Arch Linux .install script containing post-install and post-upgrade hooks. The script defines a helper function `_usb_net_hint()` that checks whether systemd-networkd or NetworkManager is enabled, and if neither is active, it prints a message suggesting the user enable systemd-networkd for USB phone tethering. No commands are executed beyond the status check and echo output. The script performs no network requests, no downloads, no obfuscation, no file modifications, and no privilege escalation. It is a routine user-facing hint consistent with standard packaging practices.
</details>
